walkthroughs.body_html:
Principles of Chemistry — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Principles of Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Principles of Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
A primary alcohol is oxidised to an alkene by losing water.

mcqs.q: What is the product of mild oxidation of a primary alcohol?
options: Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN2 because they have more bonds to break.
A primary alcohol is oxidised directly to a ketone.
An aldehyde (which can be further oxidised to a carboxylic acid).
A primary alcohol is oxidised to an alkene by losing water.

mcqs.q: Why do tertiary halogenoalkanes typically react via SN1 rather than SN2?
options: Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN2 because they have more bonds to break.
The tertiary carbocation intermediate is stabilised by three alkyl groups (positive inductive effect), making the SN1 pathway favourable.
Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN1 because they are more reactive in every way.
A primary alcohol is oxidised to an alkene by losing water.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hydrocarbon”?
options: Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.
Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.
Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.
Saturated hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — all single bonds.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Crude oil”?
options: Contains only single C–C bonds; cannot add more atoms across a bond.
Complete: alkane + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Incomplete: produces CO and soot.
Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.
Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.
